title: H1 MAJOR: keyboard/overlay routing — deck Esc-dismiss + bridge F9 stop_propagation
description:
MAJOR (2 findings). Keyboard/overlay event-routing correctness in the composed apps.
(a) Command deck cannot be dismissed with Esc once its autofocused input holds focus: the deck input (command_deck.rs:737-751) handles only Enter; a real Esc targets the INPUT, event_target_is_text_entry (shell.rs:45) is true, route_key returns SuppressedByTextEntry (keyboard.rs:650), shell early-returns (shell.rs:388) before OverlayModel::escape(). The deck also has no backdrop-click and no close button, so Esc-dead = no pure-cancel affordance. Contradicts SHELL_SPEC §1 ("Esc closes the topmost overlay before it does anything else").
(b) Bridge editor swallows F-key-exempt shell chords: editor.rs:164 `ev.stop_propagation()` runs UNCONDITIONALLY for every keydown, so F9 Recalculate (and the whole F-key exemption class, plus Ctrl+K) never bubble to .dna-shell handle_keydown in the Bench app. Defeats SHELL_SPEC §5's tested F-key exemption ("F9 must work from inside edit buffers").
Also (finding #5): the shell browser smoke `..._esc_closes` dispatches Escape on the shell ROOT div, not the focused deck input, so it green-lights an Esc path users can't take and masks (a).
FIX: give the command-deck input an explicit Escape handler that calls controls.close (with stop_propagation) — deck-local, avoid touching shell.rs guard; make the bridge editor stop_propagation ONLY for keys it actually consumes (completion nav, Enter, Escape), letting unhandled keys bubble; fix the Esc smoke test to dispatch on the focused deck input. Resolve the SHELL_SPEC §1-vs-§5 tension explicitly in the spec (overlay-with-text-input Esc semantics). Add a browser test: F9 pressed inside the Bench editor reaches the shell dispatcher; Esc on the focused deck input closes the deck.
close_reason: Keyboard/overlay routing fixed (merged d8c3cf8): (a) command-deck input handles Escape locally — closes overlay, no command run, stop_propagation — restoring Esc-dismiss; (b) bridge editor stop_propagation now ONLY on keys it consumes (completion nav / Enter / Esc-revert), so F9 + Ctrl+K bubble to the shell (F-key exemption restored); (c) shell Esc smoke test now dispatches on the real .dna-deck__input + new bridge test proves F9/Ctrl+K bubble & Esc consumed — both verified to FAIL pre-fix; (d) SHELL_SPEC §1/§5 Esc-vs-text-entry precedence documented. 55 shell + 17 bridge native + 7+5 browser green.

title: H2 MAJOR: desktop rebind/override skips hard-reserved rejection
description:
MAJOR. Desktop rebind/override hard-reserved gate hole (keyboard-conformance finding).
rebind_validated (keyboard.rs:437) and with_overrides (keyboard.rs:355) guard hard-reserved rejection behind `runtime.is_browser() && is_hard_reserved(...)`, so on RuntimeContext::Desktop they reject NOTHING — a user rebind can bind a shell verb onto F5/Ctrl+R/F11/Ctrl+L/Ctrl+W/T/N/Ctrl+Tab, which then resolves and (for shell verbs) prevent_defaults, intercepting a "never bind, never intercept" chord in the Tauri webview. register_stage_verb (line 402) uses the correct predicate: `is_hard_reserved(&chord) && (is_browser() || !is_desktop_sanctioned(&chord))`. Both existing rebind/override tests run only under Browser, so the desktop hole is untested. Module docs (is_desktop_sanctioned, profile.rs:60-63) + test desktop_allows_only_the_sanctioned_hard_reserved_chords assert the uniform-on-desktop invariant but exercise only register_stage_verb.
FIX: make rebind_validated and with_overrides use the same predicate register_stage_verb uses. Add a desktop-runtime test asserting override/rebind onto F5 (or Ctrl+R) is REJECTED while Ctrl+1 / Ctrl+PageUp are accepted (mirror desktop_allows_only_the_sanctioned_hard_reserved_chords). Authority: SHELL_SPEC §5.1 hard-reserved list; desktop re-sanctions only Ctrl+1..4 and Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn.
close_reason: Desktop rebind hard-reserved hole fixed (merged d8c3cf8): rebind_validated + with_overrides now use the same predicate as register_stage_verb — is_hard_reserved && (is_browser || !is_desktop_sanctioned) — so desktop rejects F5/Ctrl+R/etc while accepting the sanctioned Ctrl+1..4 / Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn. New desktop-runtime test proves rejection+acceptance through both write paths; verified to fail against each reverted predicate.

title: H3 MAJOR: parity CI — gate must compile/run wasm + Tauri, not just host
description:
MAJOR (2 findings). Parity CI gap: no committed gate builds/runs the wasm (browser) or Tauri targets.
run-s0-gates.ps1 runs ONLY host `cargo test -p dnacalc-arch-gates` + `-p dnacalc-strand`. The four DOM acceptance suites (tests/browser.rs in shell/bridge/bench-app/app) are `#![cfg(target_arch="wasm32")]`, so on the native lane they compile to ZERO tests and report a vacuous "ok"; no in-repo script runs them under wasm32. There is no .github CI. SHELL_SPEC section 9 / section 10 item 5 and REDESIGN_PROGRAM ("the parity CI job = browser build + headless browser tests + Tauri build, part of S0 DoD; every subsequent bead ships against it") require this. Concrete rot already invisible: `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --tests -p dnacalc-bench-host` emits an unused-import warning no committed gate surfaces.
Mitigation on record: the underlying laws have native coverage; section 10.1-4 DOM behaviors are the gap.
FIX: add a wasm lane to run-s0-gates.ps1 (e.g. `cargo test --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p dnacalc-shell -p dnacalc-bridge -p dnacalc-app -p dnacalc-bench-app` via the configured wasm-bindgen-test-runner + a WebDriver when present) and a Tauri `cargo build` of both desktop bins; fail the gate if the wasm lane is unexpectedly skipped rather than silently passing. Add a committed CI workflow that runs the four gates + wasm + Tauri build, OR record in-repo the identity of an external parity CI so "both targets" is auditable. At minimum wire `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` as an always-run compile gate even where no WebDriver exists.
close_reason: Parity gate hardened (merged 1f6ce07): run-s0-gates.ps1 now runs 5 lanes with per-lane PASS/SKIPPED/FAIL — F/P/T0, contrast, ALWAYS-ON wasm compile (shell/bridge/app/bench-app), ALWAYS-ON Tauri build (both desktop bins), + headless browser tests when a webdriver is present (else honest SKIPPED, never silent pass). Fixed a real PS stdout-capture bug found while building it. Removed the dead wait_for import (wasm now warning-clean). CI-vs-doc: documented the exact invocation in REDESIGN_PROGRAM (a bare-checkout .github runner can't resolve the 4-sibling-repo workspace — real follow-up, not invented blind). Verified on main: all 5 lanes PASS, browser lane genuinely ran.

title: H4 MINOR: gate edge-scope + vacuous desktop gate + arch-gates docstring drift
description:
MINOR (3 findings). Gate soundness + docstring drift in dnacalc-arch-gates.
(a) Edge scope: run_cargo_tree uses `cargo tree -e normal` (default features), so a build-dependency, dev-dependency, or non-default optional-feature edge on oxcalc slips every gate — narrower than the docstring/REDESIGN_PROGRAM "whole resolved graph"/"stronger than the old repo boundary" prose. oxcalc_core is a workspace dep, so `oxcalc_core.workspace = true` under [build-dependencies]/[dev-dependencies]/an optional feature in a bench/TP crate would pass green. FIX: widen `--edges normal,build` (and consider `--all-features`) for the F-gate/P-gate, OR tighten the docstring + REDESIGN_PROGRAM wording to state explicitly that only normal, default-feature edges are asserted and why build/dev/optional edges are out of scope (defensible — they never ship). Pick one and make prose match enforcement.
(b) f_gate_bench_app_desktop_has_no_oxcalc is vacuous: the desktop root's normal graph contains no engine crate at all (frontend loaded as frontendDist static assets, not a Cargo edge), so it can never fail and has no positive control. f_gate_bench_desktop reaches oxfml only via its single edge to bench-host and would pass vacuously if that edge were dropped. FIX: drop the subsumed bench-app-desktop F-gate (coverage is fully in the non-vacuous f_gate_bench_app), and add a positive control (oxfml present) for f_gate_bench_desktop so it can't rot.
(c) Docstring drift: lib.rs:89-92 says dnacalc-shell/dnacalc-bridge are "not seeded yet"/"neither crate existed" but TP_CRATES (lib.rs:93) contains both and both exist; lib.rs:14-20 says the F-gate covers "two host crates" with one positive control but tests F-gate four crates with two positive controls. FIX: update the docstring to match the code.
close_reason: Gate soundness (merged 1f6ce07): F-gate widened to normal,build edges (run_cargo_tree_with_edges + F_GATE_EDGES) so a Tauri build-script oxcalc edge can't slip; regression test proves tauri-build is invisible over normal-only but visible under normal,build. Dropped the vacuous f_gate_bench_app_desktop (no engine edge exists; subsumed by f_gate_bench_app). Added f_gate_positive_control_bench_desktop_has_oxfml. Docstring drift fixed (three host/app crates, both crates seeded). 21/21 green.

title: H5 MINOR: section-7 red-error registry liveness state unimplemented
description:
MINOR. SHELL_SPEC section 7 "red error" registry liveness state is unimplemented — dots only ever render fresh or stale.
CSS defines only `.dna-liveness--fresh` and `--stale` (shell.rs:175-176); no `--error`. RegistryRail renders Names (781)/Tables (870) unconditionally fresh, Sheets stale only on dirty calc summary (838-842); no path emits an error dot. Section 7 names three states "green fresh, signal stale/volatile, red error — computed from projections, never stored" with no phase-gate on error. The state is un-wired not un-computable: projections already carry error signals (NodeCalcStateProjection::RejectedPendingRepair/CycleBlocked at workspace.rs:2012-2013; NodeView.binding_diagnostics at workspace.rs:614).
FIX: implement the red-error liveness state (compute from an error projection; add `--error` CSS token in Strand-consistent red) OR narrow the section 7 liveness contract to the two states S0 ships and note the deferral. Prefer implementing since the signal exists. Add a test.
close_reason: Red-error registry liveness implemented: .dna-liveness--error CSS (strand red-ink token), node_carries_error() + liveness_dot_class() derive-at-render helpers (RejectedPendingRepair/CycleBlocked/binding_diagnostics -> error, ranked error>stale>fresh). Wired for tree root nodes + Tables where the signal exists; Names/grid-Sheets left fresh/stale with comments (no backing error projection at S0 — honest degrade, not fabricated). 2 new tests. Merged f1191bc.

title: H6 MINOR: contrast test omits colored-ink x paper-2 (binding light ground)
description:
MINOR. Strand contrast law: colored inks checked only vs `paper`, never `paper-2` — the tighter light-theme ground.
SANCTIONED_PAIRS checks neutral inks (ink/ink-2/ink-3) on BOTH paper grounds but colored inks (accent-ink/value-ink/prov-const/prov-ext/red) only vs `paper` for CockpitLight (contrast.rs:82-86) and HighContrast (119-123). In light themes paper-2 (#EEF2F4) is the lower-luminance, binding ground. HighContrast colored inks clear paper-2 by razor-thin ~0.06 margins (value-ink 7.060, red 7.062) while the asserted paper direction has ~8.4 slack — so the build-breaking test locks only the non-binding direction; a future paper-2 or ink tweak could silently drop below 7.0 on paper-2. theme.rs's own derivation comments claim every ink clears 7.0 on BOTH grounds. No live failure today (all pass), and no colored ink currently renders as TEXT on paper-2 (value-ink appears only as a >=3:1 dot fill).
FIX: add the five colored-ink rows against `paper-2` for CockpitLight and HighContrast (mirror how neutral inks already cover both grounds), so the crate's "a palette change that breaks a pair fails the build" promise holds for the direction theme.rs engineered. If any newly-added pair fails, minimally adjust the ink (hue held) and note it, per the H6 STRAND 2.1 protocol.
close_reason: Contrast law extended: 5 colored-ink rows (accent/value/prov-const/prov-ext/red) x paper-2 added for CockpitLight + HighContrast (the binding light ground theme.rs engineered). No ink adjustment needed — all pass (CL paper-2: prov-ext 4.87/red 4.62/value 5.33; HC ~7.06+). 26 strand tests green. Merged f1191bc.

title: H7 MINOR: stale bench-corpus quarantine docs contradict fixed-and-green tests
description:

buffer_integrity.rs:141-148 titles a section "Cases that fail today (pending upstream OxFml fix)" and its module doc (8-14) describes an #[ignore]-with-reason quarantine convention, but the four cases (150-170: inter-identifier whitespace repros) are plain #[wasm_bindgen_test(async)] with NO #[ignore] and NO reason string — they hard-assert and PASS. Referenced docs/handoffs/ dir does not exist (only docs/handovers/). Risk (inverse of coverage inflation): a future agent believes a quarantine guards still-red cases and re-adds host-side gap-fill logic for an already-fixed bug.

close_reason: Stale quarantine docs fixed: buffer_integrity.rs module-doc + section header rewritten to passing framing (no #[ignore] ever existed); repro_eq_space_a_space_a.rs header PENDING->FIXED; dead docs/handoffs + docs/OPERATIONS refs repointed to docs/onecalc/OPERATIONS.md. title: Normalize node content to a single formula field (literal constants are no-= formulas)
description:
Decision (user-directed): a node has ONE content field, 'formula'. Excel cell-input convention: a leading = introduces a formula; any other input is a literal constant that OxFml parses during bind and resolves to a typed EvalValue (number/text/logical/date/error) with Excel-aligned type inference. There is no separate 'literal value' content kind. Without =, the whole input is a constant even if it looks like a name (typing Margin = the text "Margin", not a reference); with =, Margin is a reference. Matches Excel exactly.

Scope:
- CORE_MODEL_SPEC: rewrite section 2 node-content bullet; adjust section 6 array-literal line; add a section 6 engine-prerequisite for constant-input parsing; note in section 9 grammar; line in section 5 (value entry follows Excel).
- Corpus: normalize literal node formulas in workspaces/accounts.json + meta-demo.json to bare constants (=0.2 -> 0.2 etc); keep =-formulas; keep import cases verbatim (section 10 zero-rewriting preserves Excel = text). Update schema + README. Re-run validate-corpus.ps1.
- Handover: docs/handovers/HANDOVER_OXFML_constant_input.md - OxFml accepts no-= input as a constant and resolves type+value during parse/bind (OxFunc value parsing; Excel-aligned implicit number-format inference).
- Consistency ripples (specs modelling SEPARATE literal storage/kind): interop EXCEL_EXPORT_AND_REPLAY phrasing; ux/TECHNICAL literal_value field; ux/SKINS NodeState.literal_value + SetLiteralValue/ConvertToLiteral intents; ux/REQUIREMENTS 3.6. Reconcile to single-formula model; preserve editing affordances reframed as constant-vs-formula by leading =. (May split UX reconciliation into a follow-up bead if large.)

Acceptance: validate-corpus.ps1 green; no remaining 'formula OR literal value' dual-storage language in CORE_MODEL_SPEC; handover file present; read-through.

W002 intake decision (2026-05-21):

Upstream intake:
- Consume OxCalc through `oxcalc_core::consumer::{OxCalcTreeEnvironment, OxCalcTreeDocument, OxCalcTreeRecalcRequest, OxCalcTreeRecalcResult, OxCalcTreeRuntimeFacade}`. Do not bind directly to `LocalTreeCalcEngine` or proving-floor runners.
- The document still necessarily carries OxCalc-owned public substrate types: `StructuralSnapshot`, `TreeFormulaCatalog`, `TreeNodeId`, and seeded published values. Local code may build those typed inputs, but it must not duplicate coordinator/evaluator behavior.
- OxCalc result fields required for W002/W005 are `run_state`, `dependency_graph`, `invalidation_closure`, `evaluation_order`, `runtime_effects`, `runtime_effect_overlays`, `candidate_result`, `publication_bundle`, `reject_detail`, `published_values`, `node_states`, and `diagnostics`.
- OxFml §2.1A only explicitly covers `WorksheetA1` today. TreeCalc constant-entry classification and formula branch parsing remain a coordination item tracked by `dtc-d6o.6` / `HANDOVER_OXFML_constant_input.md`.
- OxCalc cycle profile field names/bounds/diagnostic surface remain a coordination item tracked by `dtc-d6o.7` / `HANDOVER_OXCALC_iterative_cycle_config.md`.

Local layout:
- Scaffold the implementation in the spec's OneCalc-shaped crate location: `src/dnatreecalc-host` as the first workspace member.
- Keep W002 narrow inside that host crate: `adapters/oxcalc` for the bridge trait/live adapter/projections, plus `test_support` or fixture helpers for the smoke workspace. Do not build the W005 shell/UI yet.
- Add a later CLI/runner surface only when `dtc-d6o.8` activates corpus cases; for `dtc-d6o.4`/`.5`, ordinary Rust tests are enough.

First fixture:
- Use a tiny acyclic named-node smoke tree: `Root`, constant `Root.A = 2`, calculation `Root.B = A + 3` (or equivalent upstream fixture expression). This proves structural snapshot + formula catalog + real facade execution + published values + dependency graph + node states.
- Do not claim this as TreeCalc formula-text coverage. Mapping ordinary user formula strings to OxFml/OxCalc bind artifacts waits on the OxFml tree channel and broader W004 reference work.

Corpus activation:
- Keep W002 `constants/` and `cycles/` pending until the handover contracts are answered or exact blockers narrow scope.
- `dtc-d6o.8` can activate only cases backed by implemented code and answered contracts. Until then, the bridge smoke test is local Rust verification, not a corpus activation claim.

Checks:
- Current pre-workspace floor: `pwsh docs/test-corpus/tools/validate-corpus.ps1`.
- Once `dtc-d6o.4` creates Cargo: `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo fmt --check`, plus corpus validation.

description:
S1-prep follow-ups surfaced by the S0-H major re-verification (wf_331ed810-46e, all 4 majors resolved, ZERO regressions). None are S0 blockers; carry into S1 Bench.

1) OWNER DESIGN QUESTION — in-editor Ctrl+Z semantics. The H1b bridge-propagation fix correctly implements SHELL_SPEC section 5: modified ctrl chords bubble from the formula editor to the shell (this is what makes Ctrl+K work). Side effect: native in-textarea Ctrl+Z (undo my typing) is now intercepted as workspace Undo (model mutation), because the shell binds Ctrl+Z and prevent_defaults it. A user typing in a formula editor likely expects Ctrl+Z to undo keystrokes, not a model change. Affects SHELL_SPEC section 5 + the bridge editor's consume-set. Recommend: yes, text-local undo while the edit buffer holds unsaved keystrokes.

title: W011 save/reopen existing-cell edits through host-assembled output and OxDoc
description:
Implement the narrow first save path: existing-cell literal edits plus engine-driven cached-value refresh of existing formulas. OxCalc is NOT asked for output in W011 (it has no output/edit-set machinery); the host assembles the output itself via the whole-model-projection recipe - the only supported cell-edit path in OxDoc today (do NOT use WorkbookModelEditKind::Replace(CellChunk): it replaces ALL cell chunks for a sheet and a partial chunk is rejected downstream as cell removal).

Recipe: dnacalc-host-core keeps a WorkbookEditLedger of applied grid edits (it authored every seed and every OxCalcTreeGridOp). At save, clone source_context.events(), replace A1's payload with CellPayload::Number(10.0) and B1's with CellPayload::Formula { region: None, text: Some("A1*3") /* unchanged from load */, cached: Some(Box::new(CellPayload::Number(30.0))) } - the cached value taken from OxCalc's post-recalc readout - wrap with WorkbookModelOutput::whole_model_projection(events), then write_save_request(XlsxSaveRequest::round_trip(&source_context, &output), Cursor::new(Vec::new())). Surface the returned DocumentFidelityLedger through HostCommandOutcome::Saved and return bytes for download.

No silent loss is allowed. Anything outside the narrow edit scope is preserved or rejected with a visible typed reason (OxDoc rejects with UnsupportedRoundTripFeature before any bytes are written), never dropped. Future guard (record in code comments now, enforce when general formulas land post-ask-(b)): refreshed cached values sourced from OxCalc recalc must never overwrite a file's cached value with a #NAME? that stems from unseeded defined names - the save path checks name-seeding status before trusting recalc output for name-dependent cells (see dtc-hj2.14). This bead proves the OxDoc + OxCalc marriage all the way back to a workbook file. Its acceptance tests are native host-core tests over byte buffers; the browser download click-through of the same bytes remains in dtc-hj2.9 and epic closure (this bead does not depend on dtc-hj2.9). Raise/confirm the non-blocking OxDoc CellEdit handover per dtc-hj2.5 so future hosts stop shipping whole-model projections for one-cell changes.
acceptance_criteria: After editing A1 to 10, SaveActiveXlsx emits bytes. Reopening the saved bytes with LoadProfile::full() must assert all three: A1 == CellPayload::Number(10.0); B1 formula text == Some("A1*3"); AND B1 cached == Some(Number(30.0)) - i.e. the host demonstrably wrote OxCalc's recalculated cached value into the event stream before save (the stale-cached-value trap is the most likely silent failure and the fidelity ledger will not flag it). The returned save DocumentFidelityLedger contains no Dropped entries for the fixture (it has no calcChain; the known calcChain-drop policy for formula edits must not appear, and reopen assertions must not require calcChain byte-identity). An intentionally out-of-scope edit (e.g. adding a new cell C1) is rejected with XlsxError::UnsupportedRoundTripFeature before bytes are written, surfaced as typed HostCommandError. Tests are native, over byte buffers, reusing the dtc-hj2.6 fixture builder.

title: W011 prove flexible host layout with notebook plus companion skins
description:
Use the new host/Skin IR split to mount the same workbook document as either B1 notebook alone or notebook plus companion skin slots such as SheetLens and DependencyInspector. This proves that W011 is not a one-off front-end, but the reference design for single- and multi-skin hosts.

The host owns layout selection via SetSkinLayout; skins remain independent views over the same Skin IR state and deltas. Layout ownership decision to pin here: define a serializable SkinLayoutSpec (slot -> SkinId map over the existing pure SkinMountSlot) in dnacalc-skin-ir; host-core stores it and SetSkinLayout mutates it; the shell's existing CockpitLayout becomes a renderer of host-owned layout state (builtin_presets become SkinLayoutSpec constants) - or document explicitly why not. Keep SetSkinLayout out of the worker protocol; layout is main-thread view state.

Grid-interest composition: OxCalc holds exactly ONE GridInterestRegions registration per grid-backed node, so two skins independently dispatching SetGridInterest would clobber each other's window. Host-core must union the windows from all mounted skins into the single OxCalc registration (viewport + monitored).
acceptance_criteria: A test or click-through mounts the fixture as notebook-only and as notebook plus a companion sheet/inspector slot, and layout switching flows through HostCommand::SetSkinLayout (not shell-only presets). Selection and grid interest are shared through host state; a test shows both skins receive their cells after both register interest over the same grid node (host-unioned into the single OxCalc GridInterestRegions registration - no last-writer-wins clobber). Switching layouts does not reload the workbook, drop the OxCalc grid state, or recalc unnecessarily. The SkinLayoutSpec-vs-CockpitLayout ownership decision is recorded.

title: W011 add strict-grid profile fixture lane
description:

Note in the lane docs that non-full session profiles pay a full-profile re-read of retained source bytes on every round-trip save (roundtrip_baseline_events) - relevant if a later perf pass is tempted to switch the default away from full().

This is separate from broad Excel conformance, but it must be close enough to W011 that the proof does not accidentally rely on non-strict tree conveniences. Reuse the dtc-hj2.6 fixture builder.
acceptance_criteria: The A1/B1 fixture has profile-lane tests that document what opens, what is editable, what is preserved, and what is rejected under LoadProfile::full(), LoadProfile::strict_values_only(), and LoadProfile::values_only() - by these exact constructors. Expected rejections (e.g. cached-value formula edits outside full()) are asserted as typed outcomes, not recorded as unexpected failures. The lane is wired into local verification where possible and records any upstream blockers as handovers/beads, including the non-full-profile save re-parse cost note.

title: W011 align worker boundary with host-core
description:
Align the worker boundary with dnacalc-host-core. The live web_sys worker already exists (opt-in ?worker=1) and its protocol is already Leptos-free; the residue this bead removes is (a) HostSessionExecutor's throwaway RwSignals + reactive Leptos Owner inside the worker, and (b) WorkerInbound::Init carrying DnaTreeWorkspaceDocument, which couples dnatreecalc-worker to dnatreecalc-host.

Work: replace HostSessionExecutor with a Leptos-free HostCoreExecutor over dnacalc-host-core's ProjectionPublisher seam (this is what actually removes the Owner requirement). Move WorkerInbound/WorkerOutbound to depend on dnacalc-skin-ir (+ the model-neutral document enum from dtc-hj2.4: HostDocument { Tree(DnaTreeWorkspaceDocument), WorkbookXlsx { bytes } }) instead of dnatreecalc-host. Extend the protocol with WorkerInbound::Command(HostCommand) / WorkerOutbound::CommandOutcome, carrying the SKIN_IR_PROTOCOL_SCHEMA on the Init/Ready handshake; .xlsx bytes cross postMessage as a transferable ArrayBuffer alongside the JSON envelope, not base64 inside serde_json. In worker mode dnacalc-host-core runs entirely inside the worker (for workbook sessions the OxDoc source context must live with the OxCalc state - save needs both); the main thread holds only the Skin IR mirror (apply_delta) + WebWorkerDispatcher.

This bead does not gate the W011 fixture closure; it is the recorded owner of the plan's worker-alignment claim.
acceptance_criteria: The worker binary path compiles without Leptos in its dependency tree (cargo tree gate on dnatreecalc-worker once the executor moves, or on the new worker-runtime crate). dnatreecalc-worker no longer depends on dnatreecalc-host. WorkerInbound::Init carries the model-neutral HostDocument and the protocol schema id. The existing ?worker=1 round-trip still passes, and a workbook session opened via WorkerInbound::Command(OpenXlsxBytes) publishes GridProjection deltas to the main-thread mirror.

title: W011 defined-name readiness: detection now, pending name-fixture lane on upstream verb
description:
Defined-name readiness for the workbook notebook. Defined names are load-bearing for the DnaCalc thesis - they are the workbook profile's named things (the bridge to tree named nodes, the home of LAMBDA, the substrate for B1 named inputs/outputs and B3 named-path access) - and the moment upstream ask (b) bind_grid_formula lands, nearly every real workbook hits name references. OxCalc's engine already supports names end-to-end post-CTRO (name-identity edges, GridDirtySeed::Name, lifecycle reports, #NAME? self-healing per e069136e); only the consumer seeding surface is missing (upstream ask (e), co-blocker with (b) in the dtc-hj2.5 handover). This bead makes DnaTreeCalc ready to prove name support within hours of the OxCalc surface landing, instead of starting design then.

Work: (1) Author a second reusable fixture with a defined name: TheInput -> Sheet1!A1, cells A1=7, D1 = =TheInput*2 (cached 14), same OPC-part constraints as the primary fixture (no s=/cm=/vm= on edited cells; <f> text without "="). (2) Add a typed pending lane (repo pending-lane convention, NOT #[ignore]) that documents current behavior: opening this fixture yields the typed names-present note + typed unkeyable-formula rejection from dtc-hj2.6 - the lane asserts today's boundary and flips to active when the upstream verb exists. (3) On activation (OxCalc exposes GridBackingSeed.defined_names or consumer verbs): extend the host ingest translation to seed the name catalog read from oxdoc-model DefinedNameSpec, then assert: seeded open renders D1 == 14; editing A1 to 10 recalcs D1 to 20 via GridChanged; an unseeded name renders #NAME? and self-heals when the name is seeded later; and the dtc-hj2.10 save guard holds (a cached value is never overwritten with #NAME? stemming from an unseeded name). (4) Delete or narrow the names-present rejection boundary in dtc-hj2.6's open path as name support becomes real, keeping the typed note for names the translation still cannot express (dynamic names, external-workbook refs).

This bead does not gate the W011 fixture closure; it is the recorded owner of the name lane so the post-fixture milestone (first real workbook) starts on prepared ground.
acceptance_criteria: The name fixture (TheInput -> Sheet1!A1, D1 = =TheInput*2) exists as a reusable test helper beside the primary fixture. A typed pending lane asserts the current W011 boundary (typed names-present note + typed unkeyable-formula rejection; no #NAME? rendered for a defined name). The lane's activation criteria are written in the lane itself: on the OxCalc seeding surface landing, the ingest seeds names, D1 evaluates to 14, A1 edit recalcs D1 to 20, unseeded->seeded self-healing is asserted, and the save-path cached-value guard is asserted. The dtc-hj2.5 handover response status is referenced so the lane flip is traceable to the upstream landing.

title: W011 split pure Skin IR from Leptos skin mounting
description:
Create the crate boundary that makes Skin IR the stable UX protocol instead of a Leptos-bound implementation detail. Move intents, projections, deltas, identity, selection, grid interest, grid projection, and session-channel protocol into dnacalc-skin-ir with no Leptos dependency. Put WorkspaceSkin, SkinContext, registry, state handles, and Leptos view adapters into dnacalc-skin-leptos.

Precondition: commit the pending NodeClassification (C2) work in src/dnatreecalc-skin-framework/src/workspace.rs (pure, self-tested, ~230 lines) before any file moves, and re-export NodeClassification from the IR lib.rs (it is not exported today).

Symbol dispositions (verified by survey - only 4 of 18 modules touch Leptos): dnacalc-skin-ir gets identity, selection, workspace, intent protocol (Dispatcher trait, WorkspaceIntent, receipts), session_channel, permissions, manifest (SkinManifest/SkinCapabilities), command, preview trait, and the pure half of state.rs (SkinState trait, SharedSkinState/SharedStateChange/SharedStateOrigin/apply_change). dnacalc-skin-leptos gets skin.rs, registry.rs (SkinRegistry/RegisteredSkin), SkinStateHandle, SharedSkinStateHandle (Copy only via the Leptos arena), the RwSignal-backed InMemoryDispatcher, tests.rs - plus the Leptos-free-but-UI-side modules keybinding.rs, style.rs (CSS constants), theme.rs, accessibility.rs as plain modules (a B3 wire-protocol consumer must not carry CSS strings and key chords). LocalFileSkinStatePersistenceStore (std::fs) moves to dnacalc-host-core in dtc-hj2.3.

Add a signal-free RecordingDispatcher (Arc<Mutex<SelectionState>> plus intent log) to the IR crate so IR-side and host-core tests never need Leptos. dnacalc-skin-leptos re-exports the IR (pub use dnacalc_skin_ir::*) so downstream import churn across the ~25 consuming files stays minimal; dnatreecalc-skin-framework may remain temporarily as a facade with one later cleanup bead.

Add pub const SKIN_IR_PROTOCOL_SCHEMA: &str = "dnacalc.skin_ir.v1" plus a schema field on the session handshake (worker Init/Ready, future MCP hello), and document the unknown-variant policy at the crate root (serde rejects unknown intent variants - version-skewed peers get a typed decode failure, never a silently-ignored intent).

This is the enabling refactor for the reference host, browser UI, worker, CLI/MCP, and future multi-skin hosts. Aggressive rewrite is allowed: preserve behavior through tests and adapters, not through compatibility scaffolding.
acceptance_criteria: Record the pre-split test baseline first (cargo test -j 1 --no-fail-fast; 8-9 known corpus failures on main per project memory) and show the post-split run matches it. dnacalc-skin-ir builds without Leptos anywhere in its dependency tree INCLUDING dev-dependencies (cargo tree -p dnacalc-skin-ir -e normal,dev contains no leptos) and contains the serializable protocol types plus NodeClassification and SKIN_IR_PROTOCOL_SCHEMA. dnacalc-skin-leptos builds on top of it, owns Leptos mounting only, and re-exports the IR. cargo build --workspace (including dnatreecalc-worker and dnatreecalc-web) and trunk build succeed after the split. THREE_FRONTENDS_PLAN.md's hard-coded file pointers (workspace.rs / intent.rs / session_channel.rs / worker lib.rs) are updated to the new paths in the same commit. Architecture docs name the new split. New crates inherit the workspace [profile.dev] debuginfo settings (Windows paging-limit warning in root Cargo.toml).

New shared protocol behavior is tracked separately in dtc-hj2.15.

title: W011 create Leptos-free dnacalc-host-core skeleton
description:
Create dnacalc-host-core as the reference host core. It must be Leptos-free and own the root host state: active document identity, OxDoc source/model context handles, OxCalc context, dirty/save ledger state, command execution, projections, and the Skin IR snapshot/delta stream. This crate is the first clean implementation of the host pattern documented in OxDoc: the host calls OxDoc to load/save file bytes and passes the neutral model into OxCalc; OxDoc and OxCalc never own application state or call each other behind the host.

Gap-4 declaration: dnacalc-host-core IS the host-adjacent Leptos-free SessionEngine crate mandated by THREE_FRONTENDS_PLAN section A1/Gap 4 (B1 and B3 both depend on it). SessionEngine init/apply/snapshot/export_xlsx map onto OpenXlsxBytes / DispatchWorkspaceIntent / the snapshot accessor / SaveActiveXlsx. Update the Gap-4 line in THREE_FRONTENDS_PLAN.md in the same commit that creates the crate.

Command surface (typed end to end): pub enum HostCommand { OpenXlsxBytes { bytes: Vec<u8>, name: Option<String> }, SaveActiveXlsx, CloseActiveDocument { discard_unsaved: bool }, SetSkinLayout(SkinLayoutSpec), DispatchWorkspaceIntent(WorkspaceIntent) } with fn execute(&mut self, HostCommand) -> Result<HostCommandOutcome, HostCommandError> where HostCommandOutcome is Opened{document_id, load_ledger} / Saved{bytes, save_ledger: DocumentFidelityLedger} / Dispatched(IntentReceipt) / LayoutSet / Closed, and HostCommandError wraps oxdoc_xlsx::XlsxError (incl. UnsupportedRoundTripFeature) as data, not strings. Add fn document_status() -> DocumentStatus { dirty, save_restrictions }. Boundary rule: WorkspaceIntent mutates the open model; HostCommand manages documents, files, and layout. Migrating WorkspaceIntent::{NewWorkspace, SwitchWorkspace, RenameWorkspace} to HostCommand is a recorded follow-up bead, not W011 scope.

Internal ordering: (1) Move the already-Leptos-free pieces verbatim: TreeWorkspaceSession (session.rs), WorkerProxyCore, persistence.rs, projection.rs, templates.rs. (2) Rewrite HostDispatcher around a ProjectionPublisher trait replacing every RwSignal get_untracked()/set() pair (its signal usage is non-reactive, so this is mechanical-but-wide); dnatreecalc-host becomes the Leptos adapter binding signals plus SharedSkinStateHandle to the publisher. (3) Keep projection_seq assignment semantics identical (AtomicU64 in the core; apply_delta from_seq checks must not resync-storm worker mirrors). (4) Resolve the Send/Sync question before the Dispatcher trait ossifies: audit whether OxCalcTreeContext/TreeWorkspaceSession are Send; if Send, own sessions as plain Arc<Mutex<DocumentSession>> fields and delete the thread_local HOST_SESSIONS registry; if not Send, keep Dispatcher: Send+Sync for native/worker transports plus a LocalDispatcher for the wasm main thread - write the decision here either way. (5) Move build_default_registry out of the host crate (to dnatreecalc-web or a leptos-side module) and delete host's unused dnatreecalc-shell dependency.

Crate mechanics: crates live at src/dnacalc-* at the same depth as existing crates, preserving the CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR-relative fixture-path arithmetic of WorkspaceFixture::from_repo_fixture (15 corpus test files break silently if crate depth changes - or switch to a workspace-root env lookup in the same change); explicit workspace member additions; add oxdoc_model/oxdoc_xlsx to [workspace.dependencies] mirroring the oxcalc_core sibling path-dep pattern; inherit workspace [profile.dev]; host-core takes no wasm-bindgen dep (transport crates own the =0.2.117 pin).
acceptance_criteria: dnacalc-host-core compiles and tests prove no Leptos dependency (normal plus dev: cargo tree gate). It exposes HostCommand {OpenXlsxBytes, SaveActiveXlsx, CloseActiveDocument, SetSkinLayout, DispatchWorkspaceIntent} with typed HostCommandOutcome/HostCommandError and document_status(). The oxdoc wasm spike is run and its result recorded in this bead: after adding oxdoc_model/oxdoc_xlsx to [workspace.dependencies], run cargo check -p oxdoc-model -p oxdoc-xlsx --target wasm32-unknown-unknown from this workspace; on failure, raise/extend the OxDoc handover (dtc-hj2.5) requesting a wasm-lean zip feature selection BEFORE dtc-hj2.9 starts, and add that handover-response dependency to dtc-hj2.9. THREE_FRONTENDS_PLAN Gap-4 line updated in the same commit. The Send/Sync decision and projection_seq semantics are documented in-crate. dnatreecalc-host either delegates to the core or has a documented transitional wrapper; the existing ?worker=1 round-trip still passes (no mirror resync storm).

title: W011 introduce model-neutral session abstractions
description:
Refactor the current tree-specific session shape into model-neutral host sessions - as a closed enum, not a trait. Introduce pub enum DocumentSession { RichTree(RichTreeSession), Workbook(WorkbookSession) } in dnacalc-host-core. TreeWorkspaceSession (scenarios, sweeps, revision cursors, .dnatree persistence) and WorkbookSession (HostOwnedXlsxSource plus OxCalc grid state plus edit ledger) share almost no lifecycle beyond "consume WorkspaceIntent, publish WorkspaceState" - that pair IS CalcModelSession for now; extract a trait only when a third model family exists. WorkbookSession is the target for .xlsx strict-grid documents; RichTreeSession preserves the tree-model surface through the new core.

Host-core matches per intent/command and returns a typed IntentError::UnsupportedByModel receipt for intents a family does not support (e.g. CreateScenario on Workbook). W011 WorkbookSession returns UnsupportedByModel for Undo/Redo (the WorkbookEditLedger from dtc-hj2.10 is the future workbook-undo substrate, noted as a follow-up bead); workbook dirty = edit ledger non-empty since last successful SaveActiveXlsx, exposed via document_status().

The point is to drop tree-specific assumptions from the core bits now, while the repo still has no legacy compatibility constraints, without freezing a premature abstraction. The host should be able to mount a single skin or multiple skins over either model family through the same Skin IR protocol.
acceptance_criteria: The host core represents a tree workspace and a workbook workspace through DocumentSession without tree-specific types leaking into Skin IR protocol names. Existing tree flows still compile through RichTreeSession. WorkbookSession has enough skeleton state for open/edit/calc/save beads to attach (source context handle, OxCalc grid composition, edit ledger, dirty flag). Unsupported intents on a model family return typed UnsupportedByModel receipts, covered by a test (e.g. Undo on Workbook).

title: W011 raise OxCalc/OxDoc workbook ingest and edit handovers
description:
Create the cross-repo asks needed for the proof without editing sibling repos from DnaTreeCalc, ranked by verified criticality (survey 2026-07-02). Two files, per docs/handovers/README.md conventions (Status/Target/Ask/Context/Evidence header; numbered asks; response appended to the same file):

(1) HANDOVER_OXCALC_oxdoc_model_workbook_ingest.md. Ranks ask (b) - a public bind_grid_formula(source_text, channel, address, bounds) -> Result<GridFormulaCell, _>, wrapping the existing pub(super) bind_grid_formula_for_transform recipe (key = BoundFormula.formula_template_identity.key; re-verified 2026-07-04 at optimized_sheet.rs:7241 on e069136e, signature unchanged by CTRO) - as the SOLE W011-relevant hard blocker (needed for general workbooks, not the fixture). Records the local fallback per ask: (a) neutral ingest - host-side DocumentEvent -> GridBackingSeed translation in dnacalc-host-core (both type surfaces are public; the long-term OxCalc-owned ingest lane with its new OxCalc->oxdoc-model dependency edge and axis-state gaps is raised for owner ratification, not waited on); (c) authored readout - host-side authored mirror keyed by ExcelGridCellAddress (upstream ask: extend OxCalcTreeGridCellReadout with authored: Option<GridAuthoredCell> plus derived per-cell editability); (d) output production - host-assembled whole_model_projection (upstream ask downgraded to an authored-cells-changed-since-epoch readout, only if the mirror proves fragile). Ask (e), defined-name seeding, is the SECOND hard blocker, ranked immediately behind (b) - the handover explicitly asks OxCalc to land (b) and (e) TOGETHER: GridOptimizedSheet::set_defined_name/set_sheet_defined_name/set_dynamic_defined_name are pub but unreachable through OxCalcTreeContext/GridBackingSeed, and as of e069136e formulas referencing unseeded names deterministically evaluate to #NAME? (Excel-faithful, self-healing). Landing (b) without (e) unblocks almost nothing in practice: nearly every real workbook uses defined names, names are the workbook profile's named things (the bridge to tree named nodes, the home of LAMBDA, the literate-notebook substrate for B1/B3), and #NAME? is a legitimate Excel value so a host cannot distinguish "broken name in the file" from "names never seeded". The engine side is already complete post-CTRO (name-identity edges, GridDirtySeed::Name, lifecycle reports, self-healing); the ask is thin consumer plumbing - a defined_names field on GridBackingSeed (workbook/sheet-scoped + dynamic) or consumer-level verbs wired to the existing sheet setters. Timing: the CTRO rework LANDED at e069136e - consumer surface untouched, all four consumer grid tests pass on HEAD, so ask (b) is no longer sequence-blocked and can be implemented upstream immediately; stash@{0} (unreviewed, touches consumer.rs) is the only outstanding overlap. The handover still specifies contracts (signatures), not file locations.

(2) HANDOVER_OXDOC_workbook_save_contract_confirm.md - confirm-shaped: confirm WorkbookModelOutput::whole_model_projection + XlsxSaveRequest::round_trip / write_save_request express existing-cell literal edits and cached-value refresh with no silent ledger drops, and that oxdoc-model/oxdoc-xlsx compile for wasm32 byte-slice (Cursor) sources; raise the granular WorkbookModelEditKind::CellEdit modeled edit and a wasm-lean zip feature selection as non-blocking follow-ups (CellEdit so future hosts stop shipping whole-model projections for one-cell changes; zip features only if the dtc-hj2.3 wasm spike fails).

Both handovers include the acceptance fixture (A1=7 / B1==A1*3 round trip: ingest -> readout shows B1 formula text -> edit A1 -> recalc -> output carries the literal edit and refreshed cached value; unsupported edits rejected with typed reason) and an Expected disposition section (part coordinate: API shape; part confirm: existing surface reuse). Line-number evidence is re-verified at authoring time, not copied from the 2026-06-29 lane-ledger audit.

Also register the upstream surface once, authoritatively: add a lane row (e.g. [U-INGEST] | OxCalc | P1 | the four asks above with (b) starred as the W011 blocker | interim honest fallback: host-side translation/mirror per this handover | Unblocks: general-workbook scope of dtc-hj2.6/.8/.10, B1-over-workbook) to docs/interop/UPSTREAM_OX_LANES.md section C3, classified as a CALC lane with the W011 fixture round-trip as its fidelity proof - so the ledger's critical-path analysis stays true and upstream owners triaging from the ledger see the asks.
acceptance_criteria: docs/handovers contains HANDOVER_OXCALC_oxdoc_model_workbook_ingest.md and HANDOVER_OXDOC_workbook_save_contract_confirm.md, each with the Status/Target/Ask/Context/Evidence header, numbered "What DnaCalc needs" asks, the A1=7/B1==A1*3 acceptance fixture, and an Expected disposition section; both are listed under Authored: in docs/handovers/README.md. The OxCalc handover ranks ask (b) public formula binding as the sole hard blocker and records the local fallback boundary for asks (a), (c), (d). A [U-INGEST]-style lane row exists in docs/interop/UPSTREAM_OX_LANES.md section C3 naming the asks and what they unblock (or the ledger carries an explicit note that W011 ingest coordination lives in handovers only - registering is preferred). The W011 plan doc's Upstream Work section stays consistent with the handover text. No sibling repo files are modified. Later W011 beads' dependency edges to this bead mean "the handover documents exist to be cited", never "upstream landed".

title: W011 implement .xlsx open through OxDoc full profile into OxCalc
description:
Implement the first workbook open command in the reference host. OpenXlsxBytes calls oxdoc_xlsx::open_host_owned_xlsx_source(Cursor::new(bytes), LoadProfile::full()), retains the host-owned source context / model context / load ledger, and publishes a Skin IR workbook/grid projection. The host owns the root context throughout. The first fixture is deliberately small: A1 literal 7 and B1 formula =A1*3. This is not a file import preview; it is the first married OxDoc + OxCalc host execution path.

Local ingest strategy (do NOT wait for the OxCalc ingest handover to land - no OxCalc workbook-context type exists and none is needed): dnacalc-host-core owns the translation from oxdoc-model to OxCalc types. Walk the DocumentEvent stream (or implement oxdoc_model::OxCalcIngestSink and use drive_oxcalc_ingest_from_model_access) and build one oxcalc_core GridBackingSeed per sheet; model the workbook as one OxCalc workspace with one grid-backed node per sheet via OxCalcTreeContext::set_node_grid (grid_id = "{workbook_id}:{sheet_id}"). Translation rules: resolve the StringTable event before SharedText(u32) cells; map Error(u8) to WorksheetErrorCode; xlsx <f> text has NO leading "=" while GridFormulaCell.source_text convention is "="-prefixed - normalize explicitly; map MergedCellRegions to Vec<GridRect> and TableSpec to GridTableOverlay. The reference choreography is OxCalc's consumer test grid_edit_setcell_and_fillrange_publish_and_bump_epochs (create_workspace -> add_node per sheet -> set_node_grid -> register_grid_interest -> apply_grid_edit -> poll_grid_changes).

Formula keying is fixture-scoped: B1 is seeded as GridFormulaCell::new("=A1*3", key) with the key behind a single named const W011_FIXTURE_NORMAL_FORM_KEY = "excel.grid.v1:cell:R[0]C[-1]*3" (the exact pair proven in OxCalc's own consumer test, re-verified passing on e069136e post-CTRO), with a follow-up bead to delete it when the OxCalc bind_grid_formula API lands. The ingest code MUST return a typed error (not a guessed key) for any formula cell it cannot hand-key, with a comment naming the dtc-hj2.5 OxCalc binding handover as the unblock. Do not reimplement normal_form_key derivation host-side, and do not copy the attach_demo_grid keying pattern (its key is engine-harmless because normal_form_key is opaque/never parsed, but it misdescribes the source reference, and CTRO deepened the key's role as formula-template identity - wrong hand-keys silently poison plan caches).

Defined names (post-CTRO fact, e069136e): there is no consumer-level defined-name seeding, and formulas referencing unseeded names deterministically evaluate to #NAME? (self-healing if the name appears later). The fixture has no names, but this bead owns the W011 boundary: read the defined-name catalog from the OxDoc model context at open (oxdoc-model DefinedNameSpec - purely local) and surface names-present as a typed open note; name-using formulas fall under the existing typed unkeyable-formula rejection. A W011 open must never render #NAME? for a name the file actually defines - that ambiguity (broken name vs never-seeded) is exactly what the typed note prevents. Seeding itself is upstream ask (e) (co-blocker with (b), see dtc-hj2.5); the prepared activation lane is dtc-hj2.14.

This bead also owns the authored-metadata Skin IR extension that dtc-hj2.7 consumes: GridCellProjection gains authored: Option<GridAuthoredCellProjection> { kind: Empty|Literal|Formula, source_text: Option<String>, source_channel, editable: bool }. Because OxCalc exposes no consumer-level authored readout (handover ask c), the host populates this from its own authored mirror keyed by ExcelGridCellAddress, updated at seed time and on every applied edit. Spill ghost-cell values are not published by grid_view and are out of W011 scope.
acceptance_criteria: The fixture .xlsx is authored in this repo as raw OPC part strings zipped at test time ([Content_Types].xml, _rels/.rels, xl/workbook.xml, xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels, xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml). title: W011 render read-only B1 notebook from workbook GridProjection
description:
Build the first visible B1 notebook skin for workbook sessions. It renders sheets/cells from Skin IR GridProjection and the authored metadata added by dtc-hj2.6 (kind/source_text/editable - do not invent a separate metadata channel), using SetGridInterest to subscribe to windows and GridChanged/GridOverlaysChanged to update. Relation to THREE_FRONTENDS_PLAN B1 (one cell model, two substrates - do not fork): authored cell kind (empty/literal/formula) aligns with NodeContentKind; the C2 classification tint applies to grid cells only once U-DEP-grade dependency metadata reaches grid projections and is explicitly OUT of the W011 read-only slice - do not re-derive an ad-hoc classifier; EditGridCell (dtc-hj2.8) is mutation surface (1) applied to grid cells.

Reuse SheetLens machinery: grid_surface/grid_interest_window for windowed rendering and the session_channel::apply_delta in-place GridChanged mirror. Add scroll/interest coalescing (SheetLens dispatches SetGridInterest per scroll event today; coalesce before worker-mode use, mirroring the PendingIntentQueue EditContentDeferred pattern). Skin state (scroll, collapse, layout) persists through the THREE_FRONTENDS_PLAN section A2 interim SkinStatePersistenceStore, targeting the CustomXml store later - never a new ad-hoc store (Gap 5 single schema-version rule).

The skin must depend only on Skin IR plus dnacalc-skin-leptos adapters; it must not call OxDoc, OxCalc, file APIs, or host internals directly.

Skin state persists via the sanctioned A2 interim store, not a new one.

title: W011 implement EditGridCell intent and OxCalc recalc loop
description:
Add workbook cell editing through the Skin IR write side. Extend WorkspaceIntent with EditGridCell { grid, row, col, content } and route it in the host to OxCalc apply_grid_edit(OxCalcTreeGridOp::SetCell); OxCalc owns recalculation; the host updates projections (and its authored mirror) via poll_grid_changes and emits GridChanged for affected windows.

W011 scope: EditGridCell accepts LITERAL content only (numbers, text). Content beginning with "=" is answered with a typed rejection receipt (kind: FormulaEditingNotYetSupported) - never silently ignored - with a code comment citing the two independent blockers: (a) the dtc-hj2.5 OxCalc binding handover (no public formula binding; normal_form_key derivation is pub(super)), and (b) OxDoc validate_roundtrip_formula_policy, which rejects formula additions/text changes in round-trip save. Empty content is likewise rejected with a typed receipt: OxCalc has no consumer-level ClearCell verb (OxCalcTreeGridOp is SetCell/FillRange only). Read-only formula-result/spill/table constraints are enforced by OxCalc/host receipts rather than by skin-specific guesses.

Post-CTRO recalc notes: OxCalc's dirty recalc now runs over the effective dependency graph (dependency-ordered; forward chains recalc correctly), and effective-graph cycles are reported as GridRefError::EffectiveDependencyCycleDetected (iterative convergence is parked upstream) - if an edit surfaces that error, the host returns it as a typed receipt, never spins or retries. The optimized engine's warm-no-op token means "None => must recalc", never an error.

Future shape (documented, not built here): edit classification at intent time into SaveExpressible (literal edit on existing cell; cached-value refresh of existing formula) vs SaveRestricted (new formula, formula-text change, styled-cell edit), with SaveRestricted accepted into the live model but reflected in DocumentStatus.save_restrictions and rejected typed at SaveActiveXlsx. W011 ships the literal-only scope plus typed rejections.
acceptance_criteria: Editing A1 from 7 to 10 through the notebook dispatches EditGridCell, OxCalc recalculates B1 to 30, and the host emits a GridChanged delta consumed by the notebook; tests assert the delta and value change without direct skin access to OxCalc. A serde round-trip test covers the new WorkspaceIntent::EditGridCell variant. The compile-forced delta_coverage_is_total decision resolves EditGridCell results to the existing in-place-applicable GridChanged, and a test applies the delta via session_channel::apply_delta on a mirror. Typing "=A1+1" yields the typed FormulaEditingNotYetSupported receipt, visibly surfaced in the notebook; empty content yields its typed rejection. The host authored mirror reflects the new A1 literal after the edit.

title: S1.1 In-editor undo: text-local while editing (owner-ratified) — bridge + SHELL_SPEC
description:
OWNER-RATIFIED (2026-07-12, supersedes bead dtc-dpo item 1): in-editor undo/redo is TEXT-LOCAL WHILE EDITING. While a formula edit buffer holds uncommitted keystrokes (the buffer is dirty vs the committed source), Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z operate on the TEXT (native textarea undo of the user's typing) and must NOT reach the shell as workspace Undo/Redo. Once the buffer is committed/clean (matches the source), Ctrl+Z resumes doing model Undo (bubbles to the shell as today).

WHY: the H1b bridge-propagation fix (correctly per SHELL_SPEC section 5) lets modified ctrl chords bubble from the editor to the shell (this is what makes Ctrl+K work) — a side effect was that in-textarea Ctrl+Z became workspace Undo, surprising in a text editor. Owner chose text-local-while-editing.

SCOPE:
- src/dnacalc-bridge/src/editor.rs: extend the editor's consume-set so that Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z are consumed locally (native textarea undo/redo, stop_propagation) WHEN the buffer is dirty; when the buffer is clean, let them bubble (do not stop_propagation) so the shell's Undo/Redo verbs fire. "Dirty" = editor buffer text != the committed source_text the surface carries. Do NOT prevent_default when consuming native undo (the browser's textarea undo IS the effect) — verify the correct combination so native undo actually happens while propagation is stopped.
- docs/ux/redesign/SHELL_SPEC.md section 5: add the carve-out clause — an active/dirty host edit buffer keeps Undo/Redo (and only those, this phase) text-local; once clean they bubble. Keep consistent with the existing section 1 Esc-precedence + section 5 propagation clauses.
- Keep Ctrl+K and F9 bubbling regardless of dirty state (unchanged).
TESTS (fail-pre-fix, real behavior): a bridge browser test proving Ctrl+Z is consumed (does not bubble) while the buffer is dirty and DOES bubble when clean; a native/unit test of the dirty-vs-clean consume decision if the logic is extractable. Do NOT weaken to a vacuous assert.
NOTE: clipboard (Ctrl+X/C/V) stays as-is this phase (owner chose undo-only carve-out, not the broader clipboard variant).
ACCEPTANCE: cargo test -p dnacalc-bridge green native + browser; the composed bench-app still authors a formula end-to-end; commit with trailer.
close_reason: Text-local undo carve-out landed (merged 3cc1464, owner-ratified): Ctrl+Z/Y/Shift+Z consumed locally (native textarea undo, stop_propagation ONLY — never prevent_default, so browser native undo still fires) while buffer dirty (buffer != committed source, reusing existing echo-tracking; one definition of dirty); bubble to shell Undo/Redo when clean. Ctrl+K/F9 bubble regardless. SHELL_SPEC section 5 carve-out added. 3 native + 2 browser tests VERIFIED fail-pre-fix (stashed editor.rs -> real assertion failures -> restored -> green). 19 bridge native + 7 browser + bench-app end-to-end all green.

title: S1.3 Bench X-Ray: F8 panel, partial-eval pills, ring-out, drill, array windows
description:

All the IR read-surfaces already exist on the OneFormula document (FormulaDrillSurface, ArrayWindowProjection, CalcValueProjection, syntax_runs with token spans) and the bridge already renders tokens/completion/diagnostics — this bead adds the X-Ray interaction + panel.

SCOPE (bench-app + bridge, TP-pure):
- F8 toggles a dockable X-Ray panel (BENCH section 2 layout; keyboard per section 9). Renders FormulaDrillSurface as drill rows: expression text, state chip (Pending/Evaluated/Bound/Skipped/Opaque/Blocked/Error), value preview, argument name/role; array rows page via RequestDrillArrayWindow (64x64 cap honored). title: Skin IR: OneFormula format-authoring write verbs
description:
Skin IR (T0, dnacalc-skin-ir/src/formula.rs): add six OneFormulaIntent write verbs + a minimal authoring payload.

Add to OneFormulaIntent:
- SetFontAttributes { formula_space_id, font_color: Option<String> }  // None/empty => inherit
- SetFillAttributes { formula_space_id, fill_color: Option<String> }
- SetLocale { formula_space_id, locale_language_tag: String }         // workspace-scoped effect (matches FormattingSurface.locale_language_tag, which reads ambient.language_tag)
- SetDate1904 { formula_space_id, date1904: bool }                    // per-formula
- SetConditionalFormatRule { formula_space_id, rule_index: Option<usize>, rule: ConditionalFormatRuleAuthoring }  // None appends, Some(i) replaces
- RemoveConditionalFormatRule { formula_space_id, rule_index: usize }

New authoring struct (serde, snake_case) — the honest cell_value operator slice OxFml evaluates today:
  pub struct ConditionalFormatRuleAuthoring { rule_kind: String, operator: Option<String>, thresholds: Vec<String>, font_color: Option<String>, fill_color: Option<String> }
Keep it a plain small struct (avoid inflating OneFormulaIntent's largest variant — watch dtc-48eb large_enum_variant; box if needed). Read model FormattingSurface stays unchanged (CQRS split: SetNumberFormat already doesn't reuse it).

Tests (native, fail-pre-fix): serde round-trip for each new variant + the authoring struct; assert tag names are snake_case and stable. Build dnacalc-skin-ir clean; do not add new clippy -D warnings.

description:

- Diagnostics: span underlines + list from FormulaDiagnosticProjection (severity/stage vocabulary from the IR).
- Completion popup: px-anchored from CompletionSurface; Up/Down/Enter/Esc; emits proposal_id. Signature help + function help panes.

- DEGRADE MODE (pre-G1 Calc contexts, SHELL_SPEC section 6): plain-text editing + rejection spans (GridEntryDiagnosticProjection) + optional PreviewService dry-bind diagnostics; NO fake token colors (test: degrade mode renders zero token-role classes).
TESTS: native unit tests from golden fixture src/dnacalc-skin-ir/fixtures/one_formula.json (token snapshot, caret mapping, completion payload, diagnostics spans); degrade tests; verbatim passthrough; browser test typing -> event stream assertions.

title: W004 remove DnaTreeCalc formula-scanner consumption
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run the DnaTreeCalc forbidden-boundary scan over src, docs, docs/test-corpus, and docs/test-runs for legacy OxCalc formula/table scanner APIs.

Every DnaTreeCalc use of OxCalc public formula-text or structured-table scanner APIs is a migration defect. DnaTreeCalc must submit formula_text and table edits through OxCalcTreeContext only, and must not parse, query, rewrite, or lower authored formula syntax.

1. DnaTreeCalc product and active corpus paths build their workspaces through OxCalcTreeContext and assert context values, diagnostics, table views, dependency facts, and invalidation facts.

3. Scanner-backed children, ordered, and table corpus evidence is either regenerated through OxFml host packets plus OxCalc resolver outputs or explicitly marked migration-only until replaced.
4. DnaTreeCalc contains no local TreeCalc formula parsing or semantic mirror.
